advanced/custom-themes.title: Custom themes
advanced/custom-themes.description: A visual language that belongs to your product.

advanced/forms.title: Form integration
advanced/forms.description: Native form behavior, with deliberate callback contracts.
advanced/forms.content:
## Uncontrolled forms

Named native fields work with FormData and browser validation. Uncontrolled Checkbox, Select and TextField use native reset. State-backed Slider, RadioGroup, Rating and Toggle synchronize with the owning form's reset event. Controlled values remain the application's responsibility.

## Callback shapes

TextField, Checkbox and Select pass native React change events. Slider, Rating and Pagination pass numbers. Toggle and Accordion pass booleans. RadioGroup and SegmentedControl pass strings. Tabs uses onValueChange. These differences preserve the existing contracts.

## React Hook Form

Hook-form is not a runtime library dependency. Register native fields directly. Use Controller for boolean/numeric/string callbacks, mapping field.value and field.onChange explicitly. The repository's form integration story demonstrates this pattern.

## Read-only and disabled

Disabled controls are omitted from form data. Read-only TextField, RadioGroup and Toggle keep values without allowing changes. Rating readOnly is a display summary and is not submitted. Native Select has no readOnly semantics; show a summary or use a hidden field deliberately.

## Errors

Pass error to TextField or Select for visible, linked validation text. For groups, link an external error region with aria-describedby and aria-invalid. Keep server validation authoritative.

advanced/migration.title: Migration from 0.1.7
advanced/migration.description: Preserved entry points, more deliberate behavior.
advanced/migration.content:
## Package imports stay the same

Continue importing components from luminescent and CSS from luminescent/style.css. Existing component names, prop types and legacy aliases remain exported. No new version has been published by this work.

## Intentional behavior corrections

- Button defaults to type="button". Set type="submit" explicitly for form submissions.
- SegmentedControl represents a radio selection group. Its tabs prop is preserved; use the new Tabs component for tab/panel relationships.
- RadioGroup generates a unique name unless you supply one, supports defaultValue, and calls onChange once per selection.
- Card cursor spotlight is opt-in with spotlight. It stops for reduced motion.
- The library stylesheet no longer includes Tailwind preflight or global utilities. Applications should supply their own reset and layout styles.
- Repeated injected glow styles are replaced by shared, namespaced CSS. Deep selectors targeting previous internal divs need adjustment.
- Motion, Lucide and accessible foundations are ordinary runtime dependencies; only React/React DOM are peers.

## Customization

Move hardcoded color overrides to semantic --lumi- tokens. Wrap separately themed areas in LuminescentProvider. Retained TextField glowVariant values and CodeBlock language/lang aliases continue to work.

## Compatibility scope

ESM, CommonJS, declarations and packed React 18/19 rendering are tested. Browser tests currently target Chromium desktop/mobile; cross-browser and manual assistive-technology checks remain separate release responsibilities.

advanced/performance.title: Performance
advanced/performance.description: Keep the glow proportional to the work.
advanced/performance.content:
## Imports and bundles

The package provides ESM and CJS. React and React DOM are peers, never bundled. Runtime dependencies remain external and module boundaries are preserved; ESM bundlers can remove components you do not import. The CSS entry is explicit and marked as a side effect.

## Optional cost

Simple components do not implement cursor tracking or scroll listeners. Card spotlight must be enabled. Timeline uses one transform-only scroll beam. CodeBlock highlights sources up to 20,000 characters and falls back to plain text for longer input.

## Animation discipline

Use a small number of ambient effects. Avoid large blurred layers and continuously animated paint properties. Reduce motion for dense screens through the provider. The shared glow system uses stable stylesheet rules, without per-instance style injection.

## Measurement

Run npm run test:package for packed consumer, export, CSS isolation and tree-shaking checks. Exact output sizes are recorded in the architecture validation report; dependency costs vary with the components your application imports.

advanced/ssr.title: SSR / Next.js
advanced/ssr.description: Predictable markup from the first render.
advanced/ssr.content:
## Import from the application boundary

Import luminescent/style.css once in the root layout. The root package ships a use client directive in both module formats, so a Next.js Server Component can reference the library. Place state and event handlers in your own client component.

## Stable IDs and preferences

Fields and groups use useId unless a consumer ID/name is provided. Theme system preference is CSS-driven. No component needs localStorage, document or window during server rendering.

## Portals

Overlays render through Radix portals on the client. LuminescentProvider supplies a local portal container so a nested theme is retained. The server still renders trigger content; opening an overlay is a client interaction.

## Hydration

Keep words, IDs and initial controlled state consistent between server and client. ContainerTextFlip renders its first word and accessible text in server HTML. ScreenReveal renders its initial isOpen state directly, without a hidden-to-open first-frame mismatch.

## Verification

The packed consumer script server-renders every component against both React 18 and 19, then checks a bundler consumer. Browser tests collect hydration/runtime errors while navigating the built documentation pages.

components/accordion.title: Accordion
components/accordion.description: Expandable details framed by a softly illuminated surface.
components/accordion.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Accordion" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Accordion } from 'luminescent';

<Accordion title="What makes it luminescent?" defaultExpanded>
  Layered light and a fine illuminated edge create a sense of depth.
</Accordion>
```

## Options

- `title`: content of the heading's toggle button.
- `children`: expandable content.
- `expanded` / `defaultExpanded`: controlled or initial expansion state. Initially collapsed by default.
- `onChange`: receives the next expansion boolean.
- `disabled`: prevents expansion changes.
- `headingLevel`: semantic heading level from `2` through `6`; defaults to `3`.
- `glowColor`: `peach` (default), `violet`, `blue`, or `mint`.

Each heading button exposes `aria-expanded` and controls a uniquely identified region. Collapsed content is hidden from screen readers and keyboard navigation. Use Tab to focus a heading and Enter or Space to toggle it. Stack independent accordions to make a group.

components/alert.title: Alert
components/alert.description: Inline feedback with a luminous status edge and an optional dismiss action.
components/alert.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Alert" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Alert } from 'luminescent';

<Alert title="Changes saved" severity="success">
  Your workspace is up to date.
</Alert>
```

## Options

- `severity`: `info` (default, blue), `success` (mint), `warning` (peach), or `error` (rose).
- `title`: optional message heading.
- `children`: message body.
- `onClose`: shows a dismiss button and calls your handler. Control visibility in your own state.
- `closeLabel`: accessible dismiss-button name; defaults to `Dismiss alert`.
- Native div props, including `role`, `className`, and `style`, are supported.

Info and success use the polite `status` role. Warning and error use `alert`. Each severity has its own icon so meaning is conveyed through shape and text as well as color.

components/checkbox.title: Checkbox
components/checkbox.description: A native checkbox with an illuminated indicator and a soft ambient bloom.
components/checkbox.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Checkbox" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from 'luminescent';

<Checkbox
  label="Ambient lighting"
  description="A softer light for your workspace."
  defaultChecked
  name="lighting"
/>
```

Use `checked` and `onChange={(event) => setChecked(event.target.checked)}` for controlled state. Native input props, form submission, `required`, and forwarded refs are supported.

## Options

- `label`: visible label content. Provide `aria-label` when omitting it.
- `description`: supporting text, connected to the input for assistive technology.
- `indeterminate`: shows a mixed selection using the native input's indeterminate state.
- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default), or `lg`.
- `glowColor`: `peach` (default), `violet`, `blue`, or `mint`.
- `disabled`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `name`, `value`, and `onChange`: native checkbox behavior.

Tab focuses the checkbox; Space toggles it. A visible focus ring follows the selected glow color.

components/progress.title: Progress
components/progress.description: Linear beams and circular rings with a bright leading edge.
components/progress.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Progress" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress } from 'luminescent';

<Progress value={64} label="Preparing your workspace" showValue />
<Progress label="Syncing assets" glowColor="violet" />
<Progress variant="circular" value={64} label="Upload progress" showValue />
```

## Options

- `value`: current progress, clamped between `0` and `max`. Omit it for an indeterminate animation.
- `max`: upper bound; defaults to `100`. Invalid bounds fall back to `100`.
- `label`: accessible name and visible linear label; defaults to `Loading`.
- `showValue`: shows the completion percentage when a value is supplied; defaults to `false`.
- `variant`: `linear` (default) or `circular`.
- `glowColor`: `peach` (default), `violet`, `blue`, or `mint`.

The progressbar role exposes the current bounds and value. Indeterminate progress omits `aria-valuenow`. Continuous animations stop when the user prefers reduced motion.

components/select.description: A native select with a glass surface and an illuminated focus border.
components/select.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Select" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Select } from 'luminescent';

<Select label="Glow palette" defaultValue="peach" name="palette">
  <option value="peach">Peach sunset</option>
  <option value="violet">Violet haze</option>
  <option value="blue">Blue hour</option>
</Select>
```

The menu uses your browser's native selection interface, including mobile pickers and keyboard type-ahead. Use `value` and a native `onChange` handler to control the selection.

## Options

- `label`: a visible label associated with the select.
- `description`: supporting text below the field.
- `error`: validation text; also sets `aria-invalid` and connects the message to the field.
- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default), or `lg`.
- `glowColor`: `peach` (default), `violet`, `blue`, or `mint`.
- `containerClassName`: styles the field wrapper; `className` styles the select.
- Native single-select props and forwarded refs are supported, including `required`, `name`, `disabled`, `value`, and `defaultValue`.

Provide `aria-label` if you omit the visible label. Option lists can include native `optgroup` elements.

components/slider.title: Slider
components/slider.description: A range input with a luminous track, a bright thumb, and a live value label.
components/slider.content:
## Try it

<Preview><ComponentDemo name="Slider" /></Preview>

## Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Slider } from 'luminescent';

export function LightControl() {
  const [intensity, setIntensity] = useState(64);
  return <Slider label="Light intensity" value={intensity} onChange={setIntensity} />;
}
```

## Options

- `value` / `defaultValue`: controlled or initial numeric value. The default is `50`.
- `onChange`: receives the next number.
- `min`, `max`, `step`: native range bounds and step; defaults are `0`, `100`, and the browser's `1`.
- `label`: visible input label. Use `aria-label` if omitted.
- `showValue`: displays the current value; defaults to `true`.
- `formatValue`: formats both the visible value and `aria-valuetext`, for example `(value) => value + '%'`.
- `glowColor`: `peach` (default), `violet`, `blue`, or `mint`.
- Native range input props and forwarded refs are supported, including `name` and `disabled`.

Arrow keys change the value by one step. Home and End move to the minimum and maximum. Motion and transitions respect reduced-motion preferences.

foundations/accessibility.title: Accessibility
foundations/accessibility.description: Useful with a keyboard, understandable without the glow.
foundations/accessibility.content:
## Native where possible

Checkbox, RadioGroup, Select, Slider and Rating use native inputs. Toggle exposes switch semantics and participates in form submission with an optional name. Button defaults to type="button". Labels, descriptions and errors should explain what a control does.

## Complex interactions

Dialog, Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, Tabs and Toast build on scoped Radix primitives for keyboard behavior, focus, dismissal and ARIA relationships. Component documentation describes each interaction. A component is not a guarantee that the consuming application conforms to WCAG.

## Focus and naming

Every actionable element needs a meaningful name. Supply aria-label to icon-only Buttons. Use aria-labelledby when a nearby heading names a group. Do not remove focus outlines. Tooltip content supplements a label; it should not be the only place essential information appears.

## Contrast and motion

Light/dark defaults adjust text and status colors. Forced-colors and prefers-contrast receive visible boundaries. Custom palettes still require contrast testing. Honor reduced motion and give people control over cycling content.

## Validation

Automated browser checks include keyboard interactions, form reset, focus containment/restoration, and axe scans. Automated tests do not replace screen-reader checks and application-level accessibility review.

foundations/colors.title: Colors
foundations/colors.description: Warm accents, clear surfaces, meaningful status.
foundations/colors.content:
## Semantic roles

Use `--lumi-bg`, `--lumi-surface` and `--lumi-surface-raised` to distinguish page and elevation. `--lumi-text` and `--lumi-muted` express content hierarchy; `--lumi-border` and `--lumi-separator` distinguish boundaries.

## Accent palettes

The built-in palettes are peach, violet, blue and mint. A provider sets the inherited accent. A component's optional glowColor overrides that accent for one component. Accent labels use a theme-adjusted mix so light mode does not place pale peach text on white.

## Status is not just color

`--lumi-success`, `--lumi-warning`, `--lumi-info` and `--lumi-danger` are RGB channel lists with theme-specific values. Pair status with text and an icon, as Alert does. Badge text should name the state rather than relying on a colored dot.

## Custom contrast

Check text contrast and focus visibility on every surface when overriding tokens. The default primary button pairs a light accent with dark text; an arbitrary dark custom accent also needs a suitable `--lumi-on-accent`.

foundations/motion.title: Motion
foundations/motion.description: A small movement should have a clear reason.
foundations/motion.content:
## Preferences

Continuous CSS animations and transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion. Set motion="reduced" on LuminescentProvider to reduce motion in just one tree, including word cycling and the timeline beam. This also configures MotionConfig for motion-based consumers.

## Tokens

Fast, normal and slow durations are 120ms, 220ms and 400ms. `--lumi-ease` and `--lumi-ease-out` define standard curves. The exported `motionPresets` provides gentle and responsive spring presets for applications that use Framer Motion.

## Controls and visibility

ContainerTextFlip offers pause/resume, pauses its timer while the document is hidden, and reserves the longest word's size. ScreenReveal hides closed content from focus. Skeleton and Progress retain useful status even with animation stopped.

## Performance

Prefer opacity and transforms. Card spotlight is opt-in, updates CSS variables directly, and disables tracking with reduced motion. Avoid attaching dozens of continuously animated examples to one page.

foundations/spacing.title: Spacing
foundations/spacing.description: A consistent rhythm, with room for content.
foundations/spacing.content:
## Spacing tokens

The scale uses multiples of 0.25rem: `--lumi-space-1`, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12 and 16. Larger numbers create section-level breathing room; control interiors use the smaller values.

## Dimensions

Control heights are sm (2rem), md (2.75rem), and lg (3.25rem). Radius tokens are sm, md, lg and full. Icon sizes have sm and md roles. `--lumi-content-width` defaults to 72rem for applications that opt into it.

## Responsive composition

Set min-width: 0 on flex/grid children around fields and code blocks. Use max-width: 100% for component demos. Luminescent does not enforce a viewport or apply global body rules.

foundations/themes.title: Themes
foundations/themes.description: One visual language, more than one mood.

foundations/tokens.title: Design tokens
foundations/tokens.description: The small decisions that make a coherent system.
foundations/tokens.content:
## How tokens work

All variables use the --lumi- namespace. The distributed stylesheet declares variables and .lumi- component selectors, with no application reset. Component variables inherit through theme containers.

## Color and contrast

`--lumi-bg`, surface, surface-raised, text, muted, border, separator, color, accent, secondary, on-accent, success, warning, info, danger and focus define semantic roles. RGB channel lists are used by color and status tokens; plain colors are used by backgrounds and text.

## Dimensions and typography

Spacing: space-1 through space-16 (documented in Spacing). Radius: radius-sm/md/lg/full. Heights: control-sm/md/lg. Font families: font and font-mono. Type scale: text-xs/sm/md/lg/xl. Weights: weight-normal/medium/bold. Rhythm: leading and tracking.

## Effects and motion

Elevation: shadow-sm/lg and glow-sm/lg. glow-strength multiplies glow contributions; zero disables them. blur, glass-opacity and border-light support surfaces. Motion uses duration-fast, duration, duration-slow, ease and ease-out.

## Source of truth

See packages/luminescent/src/tokens.css in the repository for exact defaults. These CSS tokens can be consumed independently of React. Glow intensity can be selected with data-lumi-glow="none", "subtle", "normal" or "intense".

foundations/typography.title: Typography
foundations/typography.description: A useful hierarchy before a distinctive typeface.
foundations/typography.content:
## Font families

`--lumi-font` uses the system sans-serif stack. `--lumi-font-mono` controls code. Override either inside a theme container; no network font request is required.

## Scale

Text sizes range from `--lumi-text-xs` (0.75rem) through sm (0.875rem), md (1rem), lg (1.25rem) and xl (1.75rem). Use normal, medium and bold weight tokens for content hierarchy. The default reading line-height is 1.6.

## Application headings

Components that own headings expose a suitable heading or a headingLevel prop. Choose levels according to the page outline. Avoid using a large visual font as a substitute for a semantic heading.

## Resizing and localization

Rem-based defaults respect browser font settings. Test translated labels, 200% text zoom and narrow layouts; avoid fixed-width containers around long content.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: A little light for your next interface.
overview.content:
Luminescent is a React component library with luminous surfaces, native form controls, and a shared design-token system. It supports dark, light, and system themes, plus independently themed trees.

## Start here

1. [Install the package](/docs/getting-started) and import its stylesheet.
2. [Explore the catalog](/docs/components) to choose a building block.
3. [Try the playground](/playground) to tune appearance and copy working code.

## What is included

Native inputs and selection controls, surfaces, feedback, motion components, and Radix-based Dialog, Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, Tabs and Toast. Components expose TypeScript prop types from the package root.

## What remains your responsibility

Compose meaningful labels, contrast-test custom themes, integrate validation and result announcements, and choose appropriate headings. Components cannot determine those application-level decisions.

philosophy.title: Design philosophy
philosophy.description: Beautiful by default. Accessible by design. Engineered for production.
philosophy.content:
## Light serves a purpose

A warm accent marks an action. A fine illuminated edge gives a surface depth. A restrained focus ring makes keyboard position unmistakable. Ambient light should support hierarchy, not compete with the task.

## Familiar interactions matter

A beautiful radio group should still behave like a radio group. Native inputs preserve browser keyboard behavior, form submission, validation, and assistive-technology integration. More complex patterns use established accessible foundations.

## Motion is optional

Animations never carry the only copy of important information. Reduced motion removes cycling and decorative animation. There is no mandatory cursor tracking; a Card spotlight is an explicit choice.

## A system should adapt

Semantic variables connect color, space, typography and effects. Theme containers isolate decisions to one tree. You can make the glow quiet, change the palette, or bring a light surface into a dark application.

project/changelog.title: Changelog
project/changelog.description: A clear record of what changed.
project/changelog.content:
## Unreleased

- Introduced semantic design tokens, scoped dark/light/system themes, configurable glow and motion preferences.
- Reworked native selection, labels, form reset, focus handling and numeric edge cases.
- Added Dialog/Modal, Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, Tabs, Toast, Avatar/AvatarGroup, Badge, Spinner, EmptyState, Breadcrumbs and Pagination.
- Removed distributed global reset and repeated style injection; separated runtime dependencies from React peers.
- Added searchable docs, a typed playground, generated API references, consumer checks, behavior tests and CI/release workflows.

## 0.1.7

The existing package identity/version in the starting checkout. The changes above are not yet published. Consult the repository history for earlier changes; no historical release dates are inferred here.

project/contributing.title: Contributing
project/contributing.description: Keep the details useful for the next developer.
project/contributing.content:
## Set up

Use Node 24 (or 22.13+) and npm 10+. Run npm ci at the workspace root, then npm run dev. npm run storybook opens the component laboratory.

## Validate

Run npm run check for lint, type checks, generated API drift, unit behavior and package verification. npm run test:components runs desktop/mobile browser checks. Build docs and Storybook before a release. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the complete commands.

## Component standards

Preserve public APIs, expose typed props, use native semantics where possible, compose consumer event handlers, and test behavior. Every component needs stories, a working example, accessibility notes and light/dark/reduced-motion coverage. Avoid expensive mandatory effects.

## Report issues

Include a minimal reproduction, React/browser version, keyboard steps, expected behavior and whether reduced motion or a custom theme is in use. Report issues through GitHub.

project/version.title: Version information
project/version.description: Know what you are building with.
project/version.content:
## Workspace version

The library manifest remains luminescent 0.1.7. This engineering update is unreleased. The root workspace and documentation app are private and are never published with the package.

## Compatibility

React and React DOM are peer dependencies supporting major versions 18 and 19. The build toolchain uses Node 22.13+ or Node 24. Consumers do not require that build environment in their browser application.

## Release

Maintainers choose the next version after reviewing the changelog and migration notes. CI builds docs, Storybook, ESM/CJS and declarations and exercises the packed package. Publishing uses a reviewed manual workflow with an npm token; the assignment does not publish automatically.
